purpose: Test, by a preregistered measurement, whether the sustained AICLK depression under Newton-Schulz load on the p150a matches the Doppler slow board-power control law of firmware 19.6.0.0: a gap-free load above the power budget holds the plateau mean of INPUT_POWER at the 300 W limit while AICLK sits below asic_fmax, the enabled-arbiter mask stays at its boot value, the thermal arbiters are not binding, and the AICLK telemetry tracks the effective maximum arbiter. Issue #137 asked whether a board power limit exists and ended H-OTHER because its +/-2 percent mean-pinning band was narrower than the sampling error of a gap/busy mixture. The firmware source read for this Issue shows that the board power is regulated, not capped, and by which loop, so the question becomes conformance to that law.

firmware_model.status: pinned source; semantics used to state hypotheses and decode telemetry, not measured here

source.host_readers: tt-smi 6.2.1 (snapshot smbus_telem carries every tt-umd 0.9.8 TelemetryTag as a hexadecimal word), tt-umd 0.9.8

firmware_config_table.source: SPI boot-fs table cmfwcfg, decoded read-only with pyluwen 0.9.0 on 2026-10-19; identical on both boards

arbitration.target: CalculateTargAiclk: targ_freq = MIN(effective_min_arb, effective_max_arb), floored at fmin. effective_min = MAX over enabled min arbiters {0 fmin, 1 busy}; effective_max = MIN over enabled max arbiters. The busy min arbiter is fmax (1350) while the host holds the device busy and fmin (800) when idle, so under load AICLK equals the effective maximum arbiter whenever that is below 1350.
arbitration.enabled_at_boot: InitThrottlers with doppler_en: tdp, fast_tdc, tdc and board_power are disabled; thm and gddr_thm are always enabled; doppler_slow is enabled; doppler_critical is disabled until its triggers fire. Together with fmax and voltage this is ENABLED_MAX_ARB = 0x1d1 (bits 0, 4, 6, 7, 8) and ENABLED_MIN_ARB = 0x3, as read on both idle boards.
arbitration.doppler_slow_law: Every 1 ms DVFS tick: average = 1000-sample moving average (integer division) of INPUT_POWER; error = (power_limit - average) / power_limit with power_limit = MIN(cable limit, chip_limits.board_power_limit) = 300; output = 0.0025 * error + 0.3 * (error - prev_error); arbiter_max[doppler_slow] += output * 500, clamped to [fmin, fmax]. The arbiter integrates the error, so while it is not clamped the moving average settles in [300, 301) W (integer floor of the average). When the load cannot reach 300 W the arbiter clamps at 1350 and the power is not regulated.
arbitration.thermal_laws: thm: ASIC temperature against 90 degC; gddr_thm: maximum of the 16 GDDR die bytes against 85 degC; both proportional (gain 0.2) with the same integrating arbiter update, so they sit clamped at 1350 while the temperature is below the limit.
arbitration.voltage: Static arbiter set once at init from vdd_max; it reads 1350 at idle (every enabled arbiter was at 1350 when the idle report showed index 8).
arbitration.disabled_loops: TDC, TDP and board_power arbiters are disabled under doppler_en, so a current near 200 A at 108 cores cannot act through AICLK arbitration on this firmware. The #137 and #146 question about a current limit at 108 cores is therefore withdrawn; busy current is recorded as an exploratory observation only.
arbitration.input_power: GetInputPower() = DMC-reported board power + additional_board_power (20 W), in W. It is telemetry tag 54 INPUT_POWER, which tt-smi reports as board_power; the trace column board_power_w carries this quantity, so 300 W is in board_power_w units. BOARD_POWER_LIMIT (tag 53) reads 300.

tags.AICLK: tag 14; current AICLK in MHz read from the PLL in the same update pass as the arbiter words
tags.AICLK_ARB_MIN: tag 65; low 16 bits effective minimum frequency (MHz), bits 31:16 the reporting minimum arbiter index
tags.AICLK_ARB_MAX: tag 66; low 16 bits effective maximum frequency (MHz, float truncated to uint32), bits 31:16 the reporting maximum arbiter index
tags.ENABLED_MIN_ARB: tag 67; bitmask of enabled minimum arbiters
tags.ENABLED_MAX_ARB: tag 68; bitmask of enabled maximum arbiters
tags.AICLK_PPM_INFO: tag 69; not available on this firmware (the reader reports it unavailable)
tags.throttle_status_or_reason: no such tag exists in tt-umd 0.9.8 or the firmware; the empty throttle_status and throttle_reason columns of the Q2 and #137 traces are explained and stay empty

telemetry.reported_index_artifact: get_aiclk_effective_arb_max keeps effective_max as uint32 and updates the reported index only when effective_max == arbiter value (float). A binding arbiter with a non-integral value therefore does not update the index; the report keeps the highest enabled index whose value equalled the running minimum before it, i.e. the highest enabled arbiter still at exactly 1350. Decode table with ENABLED_MAX_ARB = 0x1d1 and frequency below 1350: reported 8 -> doppler_slow (integral value); reported 7 -> doppler_slow (non-integral) or gddr_thm (integral); reported 6 -> gddr_thm (non-integral) or voltage (integral); reported 4 -> voltage (non-integral) or thm (integral); reported 0 -> thm (non-integral). Reported 8 with frequency 1350 means no arbiter is binding. Because the index alone is ambiguous, the verdict uses the independent three-condition rule below (mask, temperatures, frequency) and records the index as decoded evidence.
telemetry.recon_evidence: Issue #137 post-run snapshots of device 1, whose capture started 0.22-0.33 s after the last launch ended (the capture itself took about 0.24 s): C108 run 2 AICLK_ARB_MAX 0x7048f (index 7, 1167 MHz), C081 run 4 0x704f8 (7, 1272 MHz), C081 run 5 0x70503 (7, 1283 MHz), C108 run 7 0x70490 (7, 1168 MHz), each with ENABLED_MAX_ARB 0x1d1, maximum GDDR die temperature 64-66 degC and ASIC 74.7-75.2 degC, below both thermal limits. The arbiter had already risen from the plateau means (C108 about 1097 MHz, C081 about 1192 MHz) by 70-90 MHz in that half second, as the law predicts once the moving average starts to fall. The two C018 and two C054 post-run snapshots and every pre-run snapshot read 0x80546 (8, 1350). AICLK itself read 800 in every snapshot because the device was already idle (AICLK_ARB_MIN 0x10320, busy at fmin).
telemetry.tag_number_verification: Tag numbers are taken from telemetry.h of the pinned source: TAG_AICLK 14, TAG_BOARD_POWER_LIMIT 53, TAG_INPUT_POWER 54, TAG_AICLK_ARB_MIN 65, TAG_AICLK_ARB_MAX 66, TAG_ENABLED_MIN_ARB 67, TAG_ENABLED_MAX_ARB 68, TAG_AICLK_PPM_INFO 69. The tt-umd 0.9.8 TelemetryTag enum agrees on 14, 53 and 65-68, has no member for 54 and names 69 NUMBER_OF_TAGS; tt-smi 6.2.1 names 54 INPUT_POWER in smbus_telem. The firmware tag table has no entry for 69, which is why the reader reports it unavailable.

clock_control_model.same_tag: tt-zephyr-platforms v19.6.0, as the other pinned files
clock_control_model.pll0_aiclk: refclk 50 MHz (dtsi clock-frequency), refdiv 2 (dtsi and pll.c), external postdiv0 = 3 so eff_postdiv = 4 (clock_control_tt_bh_get_ext_postdiv: postdiv_value + 1 for values <= 16; pll.c comments: fbdiv 128 gives VCO 3200 MHz and AICLK 800 MHz). The internal postdiv and the fractional feedback divider are unsupported by the driver.
clock_control_model.set_rate: DecreaseAiclk/IncreaseAiclk call clock_control_set_rate with (uint32_t) of the float target. clock_control_tt_bh_set_rate computes fbdiv = target * refdiv * eff_postdiv / refclk with integer division (floor) and steps fbdiv one unit at a time.
clock_control_model.get_rate: clock_control_tt_bh_get_freq returns (refclk * fbdiv) / (refdiv * eff_postdiv) with integer division (floor); this is the TAG_AICLK value.
clock_control_model.consequence: AICLK is realised on a 50/8 = 6.25 MHz grid and reported floored to an integer: aiclk = floor(6.25 * floor(8 * floor(target) / 50)). The AICLK_ARB_MAX frequency field is the truncated (uint32) arbiter value. Hence 0 <= (AICLK_ARB_MAX & 0xffff) - aiclk_mhz <= 6 for every integer word in [800, 1350] (exhaustive check), and the sign is always non-negative.
clock_control_model.smoke_evidence: In the 2026-10-20 smoke runs all 28 regulated-window (word, aiclk) pairs of C081 and C108 are reproduced exactly by this formula (for example 1184 -> 1181, 1172 -> 1168, 1024 -> 1018); the maximum difference was 6 MHz, the minimum 0, never negative.

doppler_slow_dip_model.source: throttler.c (sha256 22b9360b...), UpdateThrottler/UpdateThrottlerArb/UpdateMovingAveragePower, p_gain 0.0025, d_gain 0.3, kThrottlerAiclkScaleFactor 500; the moving average is board_power_sum / 1000 in uint16 integer division, updated every millisecond from GetInputPower().
doppler_slow_dip_model.mechanism: Below the budget (C018, average about 246 W) the proportional term is positive, about +0.225 MHz per millisecond, and the arbiter is clamped at 1350. When the integer moving average increments by 1 W the error drops by 1/300 and the derivative term contributes 0.3 * (-1/300) * 500 = -0.5 MHz for that millisecond, so the arbiter falls to about 1349.7 MHz, then recovers at +0.225 MHz per millisecond and is clamped again within about 2 ms. During the dip the telemetry word is 0x70545 (truncated 1349, index 7 by the reported-index artifact) and the PLL is set to 1349 -> fbdiv 215 -> 1343.75 MHz, reported as 1343.
doppler_slow_dip_model.prediction: At C018 most plateau samples read 0x80546 with aiclk 1350; a minority read 0x70545 with aiclk 1343, each such sample a 100 ms telemetry pass that coincided with a dip. No other word or AICLK value is predicted at C018.
doppler_slow_dip_model.smoke_evidence: 2026-10-20 smoke C018 (2.0 s cadence): 14 of 14 window samples 0x80546/1350. 2026-10-21 smoke C018 (1.0 s cadence): 22 of 24 window samples 0x80546/1350 and 2 of 24 0x70545/1343 at 14.5 s and 17.0 s, board_power_w 239 and 228 W, both with a signed R5 difference of 6 MHz.

background_from_137.verdict: H-OTHER under the preregistered none_supported policy; P1-P3 passed.
background_from_137.why_the_band_failed: Plateau samples of board_power_w were a gap/busy mixture (busy current 190-205 A, gap current 100-140 A; busy fractions 0.67-0.89) with sample SD 29-50 W and naive SE 5.7-9.7 W per run, so the +/-6 W band was at or below one standard error. Run 5 (C081) averaged 290.8 W (duration-weighted) or 292.4 W (arithmetic) while its plateau AICLK was 1191 MHz (SD 3.3 MHz): the arbiter was not clamped, so this is sampling error of the mixture, not saturation. Only C018 (1350 MHz in every sample) was clamped.
background_from_137.what_changes_here: Gap-free load removes the mixture and matches the sustained condition the control law regulates; the criterion carries its uncertainty; the arbiter words are recorded per sample; the limiter hypotheses H-TDC, H-TDP and the multiple label are withdrawn because the corresponding arbiters are disabled or the thermal arbiters are checked directly.

intervention.variable: active Newton-Schulz worker core count n, as in #137
intervention.held_constant: per-core work per launch: each active worker receives 9 or 10 matrix blocks and runs outer_repetitions fixed Newton-Schulz repetitions of 12 iterations at block size 8; total_blocks(n) = round(1024 * n / 108) with divmod distribution, the #137 core-selection rule and worker pool
intervention.other_parameters: Identical to #137 and Q2: ADR-0013 configuration (BF16 state, FP32 destination, HiFi3, fused S, matrix block 8, double buffering, full DEST sync, input/R/X0 in L1, output in DRAM), 12 fixed iterations, no convergence check.
intervention.adr_0013_departure: As in #137: configurations other than n=108 depart from the ADR-0013 batch; this is a power measurement and no throughput figure from it is compared with ADR-0013 results.
intervention.l1_requirement: As in #137: every configuration must fit L1 by the board-free ledger and the pre-open preflight; per-core work is identical across n.

load_execution.definition: Each launch is one ttnn.generic_op of the prepared program with outer_repetitions repetitions executed on the device inside the program. Launches are enqueued in groups of launches_per_sync without any host synchronization between them; ttnn.synchronize_device is called once after each group. Groups are issued back to back until at least run_duration_seconds of host CLOCK_MONOTONIC have elapsed since the first launch of the first group started; the loop then stops at the next group boundary. The group count and launch count are observations, recorded per run, never inputs.
load_execution.sizing: In #137 one repetition took 0.61-0.84 ms per launch including the host round trip, with busy fractions 0.67-0.89, so device time per repetition is roughly 0.5-0.7 ms. With 16 repetitions per launch and 8 launches per synchronization one group is about 60-110 ms of device time against one host round trip of well under 1 ms. The repetition loop runs inside the program, so no dispatch occurs between repetitions; between launches of a group only dispatch latency remains, which the host cannot see and the smoke check below bounds empirically.
load_execution.why_not_137_mode: The #137 callback synchronized after every single repetition; the host round trip between launches produced the idle gaps and the bimodal power samples. Keeping the fixed work per launch and moving the synchronization to group boundaries is a measurement-tool change, not a product real-time path; the fixed-work rule of CLAUDE.md is not involved.
load_execution.workload_interval: [first_launch_start_monotonic_ns, first_launch_start_monotonic_ns + run_duration_seconds); the plateau window is relative to first_launch_start_monotonic_ns.
load_execution.overrun: The last group may end after run_duration_seconds. overrun_seconds = last_group_end - workload_interval_end is recorded; a run whose overrun exceeds overrun_limit_seconds is failed and reported.
load_execution.group_timing_record: For every group: enqueue start (host monotonic ns before the first generic_op of the group) and synchronized end (host monotonic ns after synchronize_device returns). The record is a per-run JSON array beside the trace; it is the input of the idle-fraction check.

idle_fraction_check.definition: host_visible_idle_fraction = sum over consecutive groups of max(0, start[k+1] - end[k]) restricted to the plateau window, divided by the plateau duration
idle_fraction_check.consequence: A run above the limit is not_evaluable (load contract), never reinterpreted.
idle_fraction_check.limitation: Dispatch gaps between launches inside a group are invisible to the host; the smoke acceptance below checks their effect on the samples.

configurations.role: below-budget control: the doppler_slow arbiter is expected to stay clamped at 1350 and the power unregulated

configuration_note: C054 (knee) is dropped: it was exploratory in #137 and the control-law test needs one clearly unregulated and two clearly regulated configurations. Gap-free load raises the unthrottled power of every configuration above its #137 value; C018 measured 254-256 W with gaps and the #137 estimate for it was at most 253 W unthrottled, so it is expected to remain below the 300 W budget.

measurement_scope.device_note: Same physical board as Q2 and #137. Device 0 is not used.
measurement_scope.run_duration_definition: Fixed workload interval of sustained device work; setup and teardown are outside it.
measurement_scope.run_guard_definition: Workload subprocess timeout and harness deadline: 180 s load + 40 s runner setup/teardown margin + 10 s overrun allowance. A run that reaches the guard fails and is never extended.
measurement_scope.order_definition: Sequence S followed by its reverse, so each configuration's mean position is equal and slow drift across the session cancels in the configuration comparison.
measurement_scope.trace_cadence_note: Revision 5: the sampler sleeps 1.0 s between tt-smi captures that take about 0.25 s, so the observed cadence is about 1.25 s and the 120 s plateau yields about 96 samples. The 2026-10-20 smoke runs showed a board_power_w sample SD of 23-25 W at the regulated configurations while the ASIC voltage and current were constant, i.e. INPUT_POWER sample scatter rather than load variation; at the previous 2.25 s cadence (about 53 samples) the 99 percent half-width would be about 9 W, at the precision floor. About 96 samples give about 6.6 W if the samples are uncorrelated; the AR(1) correction still applies. The minimum of 50 plateau samples is unchanged.

smoke_runs.purpose: Confirm that the grouped launch mode runs and records for each core set, that the arbiter columns are populated, and that the gap/busy mixture is gone. Smoke runs are diagnostics, not verdict evidence. 40 s is under the 60 s per-instance approval threshold; the 90 s guard (40 + 40 + 10) is a timeout, not a load duration.
acceptance: host_visible_idle_fraction over [10 s, 40 s) of the smoke run is at most 0.02 (the load-contract gate)
every sample of the trace, inside or outside the window, carries all four arbiter words and ENABLED_MAX_ARB reads 0x1d1
R5: in every sample in [10 s, 40 s) 0 <= (AICLK_ARB_MAX & 0xffff) - aiclk_mhz <= 7 MHz

R7 distribution: every sample in [10 s, 40 s) reads index 7 or 8 for C081 and C108; for C018 every sample reads 0x80546 with aiclk 1350 or 0x70545 with aiclk 1343 and the majority reads 0x80546; any other word is examined before any long run

Reported, not gated: for C081 and C108 the minimum current_a, the number of window samples with current_a below 150 A, the sample SD of board_power_w over [10 s, 40 s), and the mean board_power_w; for C018 the number of 0x70545 samples; these are compared with the 2026-10-21 values (C081 1 of 24 below 150 A, C108 2 of 24, SD 10.5 and 24.7 W; C018 2 of 24 dips) and a larger dip count or a bimodal current distribution with a mode below 150 A is reported as a change of the load behaviour before any long run

If any gated item fails, the plan is revised (outer_repetitions, launches_per_sync or the check itself) and re-approved before any long run, as #137 revision 2 did; the failed smoke records are kept as diagnostics.
smoke_runs.sample_window: All smoke acceptance items that select samples use the window 10 s <= (timestamp_monotonic_ns - first_launch_start_monotonic_ns) < 40 s, the smoke counterpart of the long-run plateau selection. Rows captured after the workload interval (the runner keeps them as diagnostics, as in #137) are outside every item; 'at or after 10 s' in the items below means within this window.
smoke_runs.revision_5_note: The 2026-10-20 smoke runs (C018, C081, C108; records kept as diagnostics) passed the idle-fraction, arbiter-word and R7 items for all three configurations with host_visible_idle_fraction 3.5e-5 to 4.1e-5, and failed the current, board-power SD and R5 items at C081 and C108. The failures were examined: the R5 residual (max 6 MHz) is the PLL grid (firmware_model.clock_control_model); the board-power SD (23-25 W) occurred with constant ASIC voltage and current, so it is INPUT_POWER sample scatter, not the gap mode; the sub-150 A samples (3 of 14 at C081, 1 of 14 at C108, all 137-138 A with ASIC power reduced in proportion and AICLK unchanged) are device-side activity dips invisible to the host, distinct from the #137 host-synchronised gap mode (100-140 A at 11-33 percent of samples with busy samples at 190-205 A). The two proxy items are therefore replaced by the direct load-contract item plus reported diagnostics; the thresholds of the long-run criteria are unchanged except R5.
smoke_runs.revision_6_note: The 2026-10-21 smoke runs at the revision 5 cadence passed every revision 5 gate at C081 and C108 and failed only the C018 R7 item with 2 of 24 samples reading 0x70545/1343. The pinned source predicts exactly these two values (doppler_slow_dip_model), so revision 6 accepts them in K1 and in the smoke item. The revision 5 smoke records are re-evaluated under revision 6 without a new run: the cadence, load and harness execution path are unchanged, and the change is to the acceptance evaluation only.
smoke_runs.rerun_after_revision_6: Not required: the 2026-10-21 revision 5 smoke records (harness 78b1b54, cadence 1.0 s) are re-evaluated with the revision 6 items; a rerun is required only if the harness execution path or the load parameters change.

measurement_scope.approval: Each run longer than 60 s requires owner approval per instance. A run after a reset requires renewed approval.

plateau.sample_selection: Trace samples whose timestamp_monotonic_ns satisfies 60 s <= (timestamp - first_launch_start_monotonic_ns) < 180 s. No held pre-window point, no padding, no interpolation.
plateau.minimum_samples_consequence: Fewer than 50 plateau samples makes the run not_evaluable (sample count).
plateau.justification: Q2 and #137 showed AICLK settled within 60 s; with regulated power the residual AICLK drift (temperature-dependent leakage) is expected and does not affect the power criterion. The 120 s window gives at least 50 samples at the observed cadence.

statistics.estimator: Arithmetic mean m and sample standard deviation s (n-1) of the selected plateau samples. This is the verdict estimator; the duration-weighted left-held mean of #137 is reported beside it as a cross-check and never enters the verdict.
statistics.serial_correlation: r1 = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} (x_i - m)(x_{i+1} - m) / sum_{i=1}^{n} (x_i - m)^2. n_eff = n * (1 - r1) / (1 + r1) when r1 > 0, else n. Degrees of freedom df = max(2, floor(n_eff) - 1).
statistics.confidence_interval: m +/- t(0.995, df) * s / sqrt(n_eff): a two-sided 99 percent interval per run.
statistics.level_rationale: Four verdict-bearing regulated runs each test containment; at 99 percent per run the nominal family false-fail rate under the model is at most 4 percent (1 - 0.99^4), against about 19 percent for 95 percent intervals. The remaining model risk (non-AR(1) correlation, non-normality) is stated in limitations.
statistics.precision_floor: A containment or exclusion verdict is read only when the interval half-width is at most 10 W; otherwise the run is not_evaluable (precision). With the #137 C018 sample SD (10-11 W) and n_eff about 50 the half-width is about 4 W; with the #137 mixture SDs (29-50 W) it would exceed the floor, which is the intended outcome if the gaps persist.
statistics.pooled_report: For each configuration the two runs' plateau samples (after glitch exclusion) are concatenated in run order and a 95 percent t interval is reported with the same estimator: n is the total count, r1 is computed from adjacent pairs within the same run only (the pair that straddles the run boundary is omitted from the numerator, the denominator is the pooled sum of squares), n_eff and df follow the per-run formulas. It is a secondary description, not a verdict input.
statistics.per_configuration: Each run is evaluated individually; a criterion passes for a configuration only when it passes in both runs.

limits.source: Read from the pre-run snapshot of each run: limits.board_power_limit, limits.asic_fmax and limits.therm_trip_l1_limit as in #137; smbus_telem.BOARD_POWER_LIMIT (expected 0x12c) and ENABLED_MAX_ARB (expected 0x1d1) as the per-run configuration check. The GDDR thermal limit has no telemetry tag; its value 85 is from the firmware config table and is recorded as such. A pre-run snapshot whose BOARD_POWER_LIMIT or ENABLED_MAX_ARB differs from the expected word makes the run not_evaluable (configuration), never substituted.

criteria.predicted_interval_basis: Integer floor of the 1000-sample moving average and 1 W telemetry resolution; the integrating arbiter holds the floored average at 300.

regulated_run.R1-power-regulated: The 99 percent interval of the plateau mean of board_power_w intersects [300, 301] W (interval low <= 301 and interval high >= 300), with half-width <= 10 W.
regulated_run.R2-arbiter-unclamped: Every plateau sample has aiclk_mhz < 1350 and AICLK_ARB_MAX frequency (low 16 bits) < 1350; the plateau mean AICLK is below 0.95 * asic_fmax (1282.5 MHz).
regulated_run.R3-mask-unchanged: Every plateau sample reads ENABLED_MAX_ARB == 0x1d1 and ENABLED_MIN_ARB == 0x3.
regulated_run.R4-busy: Every plateau sample reads AICLK_ARB_MIN == 0x10546 (busy min arbiter at 1350). Without this AICLK would be 800 regardless of the maximum arbiters and R5 is undefined.
regulated_run.R5-aiclk-tracks-arbiter: In every plateau sample 0 <= (AICLK_ARB_MAX & 0xffff) - aiclk_mhz <= 7 MHz. The firmware realises AICLK on a 6.25 MHz feedback-divider grid and reports it floored, while the arbiter word is the truncated float target (firmware_model.clock_control_model), so the static difference is 0..6 MHz; one further MHz is allowed for a tt-smi read that straddles a telemetry update while the arbiter drifts at plateau rates (well under 1 MHz per 100 ms pass). A negative difference or one above 7 MHz fails the criterion. Revision 5 replaced the earlier |difference| <= 2 MHz, which the 2026-10-20 smoke runs showed to be below the PLL granularity.
regulated_run.R6-thermal-not-binding: Every plateau sample has asic_temp_c < 90 and every decoded GDDR die byte < 85 (decoding per the #137 unit provenance).
regulated_run.R7-reported-index: Every plateau sample's AICLK_ARB_MAX index is 7 or 8. Index 9 is anomalous (doppler_critical triggered); 4, 6 or 0 names a thermal or voltage arbiter and fails the run; 1, 2, 3 or 5 is impossible under R3 and is anomalous.

control_run.K1-clamped: Every plateau sample reads either AICLK_ARB_MAX == 0x80546 with aiclk_mhz == 1350 (clamped) or AICLK_ARB_MAX == 0x70545 with aiclk_mhz == 1343 (the about 2 ms derivative-term dip of firmware_model.doppler_slow_dip_model), and the clamped pair is a strict majority of the plateau samples (more than 50 percent; exactly half fails). Any other word or AICLK value fails the criterion. Revision 6 replaced the earlier every-sample 1350/0x80546 rule, which the 2026-10-21 smoke run showed to be violated by the dip mechanism in the pinned source.
control_run.K2-unregulated: The 99 percent interval of the plateau mean of board_power_w lies entirely below 300 W (interval high < 300), with half-width <= 10 W.

preconditions.P1-control-unthrottled: K1 holds in both C018 runs.
preconditions.P2-regulated-depressed: R2 holds in both runs of C081 and C108.
preconditions.P3-monotonic: In each half of the order, plateau mean AICLK of C081 > that of C108; a fixed frequency cap would not show this.

hypothesis.H-DS: Doppler slow regulation: P1-P3 hold, R1-R7 hold in all four runs of C081 and C108, and K1-K4 hold in both C018 runs.
hypothesis.H-OTHER: Any criterion fails in a verdict-bearing run while every required field is present; the report names the failed criterion and run.
hypothesis.not_evaluable: A required field or limit is missing, a configuration check differs, the sample count is below 50, the precision floor is not met, or the idle-fraction limit is exceeded in any verdict-bearing run; the report names the field and run.

criteria.correlation_warning: A supported label means the preregistered pattern was observed and matches the pinned source; it does not prove the firmware executed that code path.

sample_glitch_rule.flag: A plateau sample is flagged as a telemetry read glitch when (a) all four arbiter words are zero, or (b) ENABLED_MAX_ARB alone departs from 0x1d1 while AICLK_ARB_MIN, AICLK_ARB_MAX, aiclk_mhz, board_power_w and asic_temp_c are nominal for that run, or (c) board_power_w is zero. A sample whose GDDR words contain a zero word while the other fields are nominal is flagged for R6 only (the #137 run 5 sample 17 case).
sample_glitch_rule.handling: Flagged samples are listed in the analysis with their index and reason, excluded from the criteria they are flagged for, and counted. More than 2 flagged samples in a run make the run not_evaluable (telemetry). The 50-sample minimum applies after exclusion.
sample_glitch_rule.rationale: Raw zero GDDR words occurred once in about 1,800 #137 words; a zero-slack every-sample rule would let one such read turn a conforming run into H-OTHER. The cap keeps the rule from absorbing a real anomaly.
sample_glitch_rule.nominal_predicate: 'Nominal for that run' is a defined predicate, not a judgement: a sample is nominal when it satisfies every per-sample criterion of its run type other than R3 (regulated runs: R2, R4, R5, R6, R7; control runs: K1, R4, R6) and its board_power_w lies within 3 sample standard deviations of the median of the run's plateau board_power_w, both statistics computed over all plateau samples including the candidate. For the GDDR clause the predicate is the same with the GDDR half of R6 omitted. No absolute power band is introduced.
sample_glitch_rule.evaluation_order: Order of evaluation per run: (1) the pre-run snapshot configuration check of the limits block (BOARD_POWER_LIMIT, ENABLED_MAX_ARB): a mismatch makes the run not_evaluable (configuration) before any sample is read. (2) Glitch flagging over the plateau samples with the predicate above; flagged samples are excluded and counted against the cap of 2. (3) Any unflagged plateau sample whose ENABLED_MAX_ARB differs from 0x1d1 makes the run not_evaluable (configuration), as prediction_mismatch_policy states; this step precedes R3, so an ENABLED_MAX_ARB departure never yields H-OTHER. (4) The criteria R1-R7 or K1-K4 on the remaining samples; R3 can then fail only through ENABLED_MIN_ARB, and that failure is H-OTHER. The same sample is therefore classified exactly once: excluded, configuration, or criterion.

expected_pattern: C018: 1350 MHz and 0x80546 in every plateau sample; board power above the #137 value of about 255 W because the gaps are gone, but with an interval below 300 W.

C081 and C108: plateau board_power_w interval contains 300-301 W with half-width about 3-5 W; AICLK lower than in #137 (below about 1190 and 1100 MHz respectively) because the same 300 W budget is now spent without idle gaps; C081 above C108.
Every regulated sample reads index 7 (occasionally 8) with the frequency equal to aiclk_mhz, ENABLED_MAX_ARB 0x1d1, ASIC below 90 degC and GDDR dies below 85 degC.
Busy current at C108 near 200 A is recorded and has no bearing on the verdict.
prediction.basis: Pinned firmware source and the #137 traces and snapshots; they inform the prediction only.

prediction_mismatch_policy: If a regulated run's interval lies entirely below 300 W with gaps absent (idle fraction within limit, no bimodality), report H-OTHER and examine the DMC power path (the INPUT_POWER additive term, cable limit) before any reinterpretation; do not widen the interval.

If a regulated run's interval lies entirely above 301 W, report H-OTHER as anomalous (the law cannot hold the average above the limit unless the arbiter is clamped at fmin) and check AICLK_ARB_MIN and kernel NOP activity in the snapshots.

If any sample reports index 4, 6 or 0, report H-OTHER naming the arbiter and compare the temperatures and voltage with their limits; a thermal arbiter binding at a temperature below its limit would contradict the pinned source.
If ENABLED_MAX_ARB differs from 0x1d1 in any sample or snapshot, the run is not_evaluable (configuration) and the firmware table is re-read before any further run.
If C018 is depressed, report H-OTHER under P1 and examine whether the gap-free C018 load exceeds the budget; do not lower n without a plan revision and approval.

exploratory.status: reported separately; never enters the verdict
items: Busy current per configuration against the disabled 200 A TDC limit.
Distribution of the reported arbiter index (7 versus 8) and of the AICLK residual of R5.
Plateau drift of AICLK against fan_rpm, GDDR and ASIC temperatures at regulated power (leakage).
Onset: time from first launch until the first sample with AICLK_ARB_MAX frequency < 1350 and until the first sample within 5 W of 300.
Lag-1 autocorrelation and n_eff per run, as a check of the serial-correlation model.
Duration-weighted plateau means beside the arithmetic ones.
Arbiter release after load end: AICLK_ARB_MAX frequency in the post-run snapshot against the plateau mean and the capture delay, as a check of the loop's rise rate.
exploratory.current_dips: Current dips: fraction of plateau samples with current_a below 0.8 times the plateau median current at C081 and C108, their board_power_w and power_w, and whether they cluster at group boundaries (group timing record); the 2026-10-20 smoke runs showed 1-3 such samples of 14 with ASIC power reduced in proportion and AICLK unchanged, a device-side dip the host cannot see (candidate: program dispatch between launches).
exploratory.control_dips: C018: fraction of plateau samples reading 0x70545/1343 (the derivative-term dips), their board_power_w, and the time between them; the smoke runs gave 0 of 14 and 2 of 24. A fraction at or above 50 percent fails K1 and would indicate that the integer moving average flips far more often than the model implies.

cooldown.required_between: every consecutive pair of long runs
cooldown.baseline_source: the preceding run's pre-run snapshot on the selected device; fail closed if unavailable
cooldown.criterion: power_w <= baseline + 5 W and asic_temp_c <= baseline + 3 degC
cooldown.aiclk_not_used: AICLK is not a cooldown criterion: idle AICLK is 800 MHz, and 1350 MHz is a loaded value.
cooldown.cap_policy: Reaching the cap stops the session; the remaining runs need renewed approval.
cooldown.note: As in #137 this is a relative gate, not a common-initial-temperature guarantee; pre-run temperatures are recorded and reported.

trace.base: Issue #137 issue-137-power-trace-v1 columns, unchanged (including the always-empty throttle_status and throttle_reason columns, whose absence of a source tag is now documented)

added_columns.aiclk_arb_min_raw: smbus_telem.AICLK_ARB_MIN, hexadecimal word as emitted by tt-smi
added_columns.aiclk_arb_max_raw: smbus_telem.AICLK_ARB_MAX, hexadecimal word as emitted by tt-smi
added_columns.enabled_min_arb_raw: smbus_telem.ENABLED_MIN_ARB, hexadecimal word as emitted by tt-smi
added_columns.enabled_max_arb_raw: smbus_telem.ENABLED_MAX_ARB, hexadecimal word as emitted by tt-smi

trace.decode_rule: Raw words are retained in the trace; the analyzer decodes frequency = word & 0xffff and index = word >> 16 for the two AICLK_ARB words, and the bitmasks as integers, citing the pinned telemetry.c lines that write them. A missing word makes the row invalid and the run not_evaluable.

provenance.firmware_semantics: The plan's firmware_model block (tag, file hashes) is copied into the archive README; the per-run environment records the firmware bundle and the host reader versions.
provenance.persisted_output_paths: Basenames or container-relative names only; no hostname, username or user-specific absolute path.

limitations: No board measurement is included in this plan.
About 2.25 s telemetry sampling of a 100 ms telemetry update; onset claims are limited to that cadence.
The serial-correlation correction assumes an AR(1)-like dependence between successive samples; the lag-1 estimate from about 53 samples is itself noisy and is reported.
Only one board is measured; board-to-board differences are not addressed.
The reported arbiter index is ambiguous by construction (see reported_index_artifact); the verdict rests on the mask, the temperatures and the frequency, not on the index.
The firmware model is read from the pinned source of the installed bundle version; it is not instrumented on the device.

revision_history.change: Created the preregistered plan: control-law conformance hypothesis H-DS against the Doppler slow loop of firmware 19.6.0.0 (pinned tt-zephyr-platforms v19.6.0 source), grouped gap-free launches (16 repetitions per launch, 8 launches per synchronization) with a host-visible idle-fraction check, six runs of 180 s in S + reverse(S) order over C018/C108/C081 on device 1, plateau [60, 180) s with at least 50 samples, per-run 99 percent intervals with an AR(1) effective-sample-size correction and a 10 W precision floor, per-sample recording of AICLK_ARB_MIN/MAX and ENABLED_MIN/MAX_ARB, smoke runs of 40 s with gap-removal acceptance. The #137 hypotheses H-TDC, H-TDP, H-THM and the multiple label are withdrawn because the TDC/TDP/board_power arbiters are disabled under doppler_en and the thermal arbiters are checked directly.

Before any harness change or board run. Added telemetry.h to the pinned sources and verified the tag numbers against it and the tt-umd enum; corrected the recon_evidence timing (capture started 0.22-0.33 s after the last launch, not 0.24 s after runner exit) and recorded the arbiter rise seen in those snapshots; added the sample_glitch_rule (flagged samples excluded from per-sample criteria, at most 2 per run); added the R5 residual and R7 index distribution to the smoke acceptance so the 2 MHz tolerance and the index decode are checked on data before any long run; added the post-load arbiter release as an exploratory item. Hypothesis, criteria thresholds, configurations, order, durations and predictions are unchanged.

Before any board run, after owner approval of revision 2, during the board-free harness implementation. The implementer found two under-specified points that would make the classification of the same input implementer-dependent: the 'nominal' predicate of the sample_glitch_rule had no definition, and the precedence between glitch exclusion, the not_evaluable (configuration) rule for an ENABLED_MAX_ARB departure, and R3 was not stated. Added nominal_predicate (built from the existing per-sample criteria and a run-relative 3-SD band around the plateau median; no absolute power band) and evaluation_order (configuration check, glitch flagging, configuration on unflagged samples, then the criteria) to the sample_glitch_rule, and specified how the secondary pooled interval computes r1 across the run boundary. Hypothesis, criteria thresholds, configurations, order, durations and predictions are unchanged.

Before any board run. The implementer reported that 'at or after 10 s' in the smoke acceptance items literally includes the post-workload rows the runner keeps as diagnostics, so idle current and AICLK after the load would fail the current, R5 and R7 items. Added sample_window to smoke_runs: every sample-selecting item uses [10 s, 40 s) relative to the first launch, the smoke counterpart of the long-run plateau selection; the arbiter-word presence item keeps every row. Thresholds and all other content unchanged.

After the 2026-10-20 smoke runs (revision 4 harness, 2.0 s cadence), before any long run; awaiting owner re-approval. (1) R5 tolerance replaced by 0 <= arbiter word - aiclk <= 7 MHz, derived from the pinned clock-control source (6.25 MHz feedback-divider grid, floored set_rate and get_rate, truncated arbiter word; static bound 6 MHz, exhaustive over integer words; all 28 smoke pairs reproduced exactly) with one MHz for a straddled telemetry pass; the clock-control sources and hashes are added to firmware_model. (2) Smoke acceptance: the current >= 150 A and board-power SD < 20 W proxy items are converted into reported diagnostics because the smoke showed the SD to be INPUT_POWER scatter at constant ASIC voltage and current and the sub-150 A samples to be device-side dips distinct from the #137 gap mode; the host-visible idle-fraction item remains the load-contract gate, R5 and R7 and the arbiter-word item remain gated. (3) trace_interval_seconds 2.0 -> 1.0 so the plateau holds about 96 samples and the 99 percent half-width stays clearly under the 10 W precision floor at the observed 23-25 W sample SD; minimum sample count unchanged. (4) A current-dip exploratory item added. A smoke rerun at the new cadence is required before the long runs. Hypothesis, configurations, order, durations, plateau window, statistics, predicted interval and all other criteria thresholds are unchanged.

After the 2026-10-21 smoke runs at the revision 5 cadence, before any long run; awaiting owner re-approval together with revision 5. The C018 run read 0x70545 with aiclk 1343 in 2 of 24 window samples. The pinned throttler source explains it: the moving average is an integer division, and a 1 W increment of the average makes the derivative term (d_gain 0.3, scale 500) pull the arbiter to about 1349.7 MHz for one millisecond, after which the proportional term clamps it again within about 2 ms; the telemetry word during the dip is 0x70545 and the PLL steps to 1343.75 MHz. K1 now accepts the two predicted pairs (0x80546/1350 and 0x70545/1343) with the clamped pair in the majority, the smoke R7 item for C018 accepts the same two words, a control-dip exploratory item is added, and the revision 5 smoke records are re-evaluated under revision 6 without a rerun. Hypothesis, configurations, order, durations, cadence, plateau, statistics, predicted interval and all other criteria are unchanged. Wording fixed in the same revision before approval: the clamped pair must be a strict majority (more than 50 percent), matching the smoke item, the exploratory item and the implementation.
